brief_summary: Three side-by-side panels, each showing a base-layer key row in warm-grey above an amber Fn-layer remap of the same physical positions: the number row remapped to F1-F12, the IJKL cluster remapped to arrow keys, and a corner of the alpha block remapped to Home/End/Page Up/Page Down. Illustrates that a 60% board's physical key count is unchanged; only the layer assignment differs.
data_sources: keyboard-layout-sizes-buying-guide.mdx § 'What a firmware layer buys back' — 'A 60% board running QMK or VIA has those same keys one layer press away ... remapping the number row to F1-F12, or IJKL (or similar) to arrows, or a corner of the alpha block to Home/End/Page Up/Page Down'
keyboard-layout-sizes-buying-guide.mdx § 'What a firmware layer buys back' — 'The physical key count didn't change. What changed is where the second function of a key lives.'
